# Without Honor: NPCs, Update 1.0.1

A Halloween update with nothing Halloween-y in it. Well, why not. The big things: a new dialogue window, interface styles and TaCZ for NPCs on Forge 1.20.1. 

## Dialogue window

I rebuilt the dialogue window in the manner of modern RPGs. Planned from the very start - and finally done.

- Three styles to pick from in "Config" → "Dialogue window": "Scene" (default: the character stands on the left at full height, the line sits on a plate, answers in a column), "Card" (old look, new format) and "Chronicle" (the whole conversation as a feed on the right). A style can be set for the whole server, and even for a single dialogue node.
- QoL: A long line is split into pages instead of scrolling. Space, Enter, a click or the mouse wheel turn pages forward, wheel up goes back. Keyboard. ↑↓ pick an answer, Enter confirms, 1–9 pick right away.
- Next to "2C" there's a new "OC" (original character) button: on this node the NPC can be shown with its own picture or model instead of the profile portrait. A new node inherits the looks, the second character and the window of the open one.
- Conversation log: the quill icon in the status bar shows everything that's been said.
- Window size: "Normal / Larger / Largest" in "Config" (not sure anyone will actually use it, but I was asked to add it :D).
- While a dialogue is open, the game HUD (hotbar, health, chat, Iron's Spells mana, minimaps) isn't drawn. A checkbox in "Config" turns that off.
- Small things: "Say goodbye" instead of the house button (this is for companions that follow you), a locked answer with hatching and a lock, crisp text at any GUI scale, and in "Open in game" you can see the window the way a player with a different monitor sees it.

## Interface styles

- Theme and frames became one choice, the interface style, and it changes every window of the mod. There are six: Original, Coffee, Space Black, Space Coffee, Vanilla (light, like Java Edition windows) and Bedrock (speaks for itself).
- The "Config" button next to the mod in the mod list opens the client settings (on Fabric through [Mod Menu](https://modrinth.com/mod/modmenu)). 

## Flags

- Flag groups in the "Player Flags" window, like for dialogues: folders with a color and an icon, multi-select, a right-click menu, drag and drop.
- "All flags" is the first row in the player list: every flag in the world and how many players have each. Sort them into groups right there and "Forget" the ones nobody has anymore.
- "Remove from player…" for all selected flags at once.

## Companions

-  "Attacks your target". A checkbox in the "Following" window: hit someone a couple of times in a row, and your companion joins the fight. How many hits it takes (ex. 1–3) is set next to it, so a stray hit doesn't drag it into a fight. Off by default.

## [TaCZ] Timeless and Classics Zero Guns

- An NPC with the "Archer / Thrower" combat style shoots a TaCZ gun held in its right hand. It picks the distance by the gun: closes in with a shotgun, keeps far away with a sniper rifle. It fires in bursts, reloads, racks the bolt and hits with the stock up close.
- It all looks and sounds like a player: muzzle flash, shell casings, reload sounds, gunpack animations (needs player-animation-lib). Out of combat the gun hangs on its back and the pistol on its hip.
- Tactical AI (on by default). The NPC shoots crouched, hides behind a wall to reload and comes out of cover for a burst, goes prone with a sniper rifle or a machine gun, lays down suppressing fire with an automatic weapon. Combat manners: "Assault", "Defense", "Cover" or "Auto". All of it is in the "Tactics" block, where you can also switch back to the simple AI.
- A second gun in the left hand comes out when the main one runs dry and an enemy is close.

# Without Honor: NPCs, Update 1.0.0

> I get modern developers who keep adding feature after feature and pushing the release back. I could do that forever too, but I think it’s finally time. The main thing about 1.0.0 is that the mod now supports three versions: **Forge 1.20.1, NeoForge 1.21.1 and Fabric 1.21.1**. All future updates will come out on all of them at once. An enormous amount of tedious work went into this, so please put this version through its paces and share your impressions and any bugs you find. But besides a ton of unexciting technical stuff, there are some fun new features too.
> 
> In the next version, I’ll go through your suggestions, polish up 1.0.0, and take a shot at the long-awaited TaCZ integration for 1.20.1.

## 🤫 Before you update
- Client and server must both run 1.0.0. 0.9.x clients can't join a 1.0.0 server.
-  Back up your world and exports. Rolling back to 0.9.x isn't supported: dialogues, profiles and presets are now saved in a new format, and NPC reactions live under a new key.

## Minecraft 1.21.1: NeoForge and Fabric
![1211](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/9820e91ac6c81e93ba5af90693bf581f8af16114_0.webp)

- **Three builds of one version:** Forge 1.20.1, NeoForge 1.21.1 and Fabric 1.21.1. Features are the same; integrations differ. Fabric has no Iron's Spells, Epic Fight or Etched, since those mods have no Fabric versions for 1.21.1. Accessories on Fabric go through Trinkets instead of Curios. Sable ships are 1.21.1 only, ragdolls are NeoForge only.
- **Files travel both ways.** Dialogues with triggers, profiles and presets open in both 1.20.1 and 1.21.1. A file from a newer mod version gives a warning on import, not an error.
- **The server config on 1.21.1 is shared by all worlds**: config/wh_npcs-server.toml (on 1.20.1 each world has its own). A world moved from 1.20.1 keeps using its old serverconfig/wh_npcs-server.toml. Delete that file to switch to the shared one. On Fabric, config edits apply after you restart the world.

## Reactions: "When → If → Then" rules
![Reactions](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/bcdbcb9597a46c3817f7e1db38cb8e1c21446f0a_0.webp)

I replaced the four old reaction lists (hurt, death, right-click, approach) with rules. A rule has three parts: **WHEN** is an event with filters, **IF** is a set of conditions, **THEN** is a chain of steps with branches. On top of that come "To" (who receives the steps) and "Frequency". The editor opens with the "Reactions →" button on the "Behavior" tab.

- **33 events**. About the NPC itself: hurt, died, crossed a health threshold, got a kill, saved by a totem, fight started and fight over, following, riding, schedule point, dialogue, trade, timer, changed dimension. About nearby players: came near and walked off, right-clicked the NPC, killed a mob, died, picked up, dropped, used an item, crafted, mined a block, stats (jumps, sleep, fishing, chests and about twenty other game counters), joined, respawned. About the world: a creature died, an NPC fell, entered a biome, weather changed, time of day (including your own HH:MM), the NPC spotted a creature.
- **Event filters**: radius, "Which player" (any, the leader, not the leader), "In sight only", creatures and biomes by id and by group (monsters, undead, bosses, ocean, Nether and more). "More ▸" holds "Every Nth time" and "Within, s".
- **Conditions**: all dialogue conditions plus 8 new ones: "NPC state", "Event creature", "Distance", "Biome", "Dimension", "Light level", "Players nearby", "Player pose". The new ones, except "Event creature", also work in dialogues and triggers.

# Without Honor: NPCs, Update 0.9.9

To put it briefly, this update made everything a little bit better and more convenient. Going forward, expect more compatibility with popular mods and - maybe - a 1.21.1 version? We'll see. Also, thank you for over 3,000 downloads across the platforms and for all the feedback you leave in the comments <3 

## Dialogues
- **Node attachments.** The "Photo" button is now **Attachments**: besides images, a node can carry a **book** and a **map**. Pick them straight from your inventory (offhand included) - only written/writable books and filled maps are accepted. In the dialogue they show up as small chips under the NPC's text. A "take back" slot gives you a copy of the book or map if you ever lose the original.
- **Choice icons.** Every player reply can have a small 8×8 icon: agree, refuse, question, exclaim, anger, heart, smile, sad, trade, fight, leave, gift, wait, home, star, secret. Pick it in the reply editor.
- **Reply editor.** Reply text is now a button that opens a proper editor with the formatting toolbar. In-game replies wrap to two lines with "…" and a full-text tooltip; the editor warns live when a reply won't fit.
- **Text animation.** A new "Aa▸" button next to Glossary turns on typewriter-style text for a node with adjustable speed (chars/sec). Click, Space or Enter reveals everything at once. New nodes inherit the setting from the node you're on.
- **"Test" is now "In game".** Instead of a fake local preview, the real dialogue opens with the NPC in a dry-run: conditions count as met (breakable buttons still break), no actions run, nothing is written to your progress, and a yellow TEST banner is shown. The dialogue is saved automatically before opening.
- **Validation** got seven new rules: goto to a missing dialogue, inverted "breakable", images without a file, music that needs a mod/Etched, replies longer than two lines, monologue pages that won't fit, broken or oversized books. Results now wrap and scroll.
- **Monologue.** `@NPC` works for both name and portrait (`{npc}` still understood), tooltips for Name/Portrait, formatting toolbar for page text, an overflow warning with a **Split** button, automatic pagination in-game, page reordering and a numbered page list.

## World
- **Redstone triggers.** Trigger blocks can fire from a redstone signal and can emit a signal of their own for a set number of ticks. Without a player in range only player-independent actions run (say, emote, wait). Should've added it right away, but I only got around to it now, heh. 
- **Spawner editor** got tidied up.

## Pets
- Edit **health, speed and jump** within vanilla ranges (pencil next to "Stats"), reset to species defaults, put **horse armor** on a horse and a **saddle** on any rideable pet - all visible in the preview.
- The **Pets** button now lives in the Behavior tab.

And a few other small things.

# Without Honor: NPCs, Update 0.9.8

A patch about things that had been getting in the way for a while: pauses in actions that didn't pause, dialogues that wouldn't save because of their size, and presets that arrived on someone else's server without their images. Plus a big pass on animation - with [bendy-lib](https://modrinth.com/mod/bendy-lib) installed NPCs finally bend their knees and elbows in [Emotecraft](https://modrinth.com/plugin/emotecraft) animations, and [ETF](https://modrinth.com/mod/entitytexturefeatures)/[EMF](https://modrinth.com/mod/entity-model-features) support means resource packs like [ Just Expressions](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/just-expressions) and [ Fresh Animations: Player Extension](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/fa-player-extension) now work on them.

> **Important:** the network protocol version was bumped again. Client and server must run the same mod version.

## Pauses and queues

- **Pause works in triggers.** A trigger block used to run the whole chain in one go: the pause was skipped and every command fired at once. It now waits honestly - including when the NPC isn't linked to the trigger or isn't loaded.
- **Pause in the on-death reaction** plays out to the end. The tail of the action list used to die with the NPC.
- **Monologues queue up.** Two in a row no longer overwrite each other: the first finishes, the second continues. And a monologue that locks controls no longer knocks you out of an open chest - it waits until you close the window.
- **Speech bubbles queue too.** Each one lives out its full duration and the next waits its turn. Nothing gets cut off mid-sentence.

## Large dialogues, profiles and media transfer

- **The size limit is gone.** Dialogues and profiles of any size save and transfer: data travels in parts and is compressed on the way, with a progress readout for longer uploads. A dialogue of forty thousand characters used to simply vanish along with your edits.
- **Images and skins travel with the preset.** Export puts them in a folder next to the file, and import only sends the server what it's missing. The file used to carry names alone, so on a new server the preset opened empty.
- **Name clashes resolve themselves:** if a file with that name already exists but holds something else, yours arrives under a free name and the links inside the preset are corrected automatically. Other people's files are never overwritten.

## Settings for server owners

There's now a separate server config: the maximum size of a single upload (32 MB by default, up to 256), the size cap for one image, and the total number of images in a world. The client sees your server's real settings and warns you up front instead of failing halfway.

## Skins

- **HD support:** 128×128, 256×256 and 512×512.
- **The built-in vanilla skins** (Steve, Alex, Ari and the rest) now come from the game's own resources. That means resource packs can see them: if a pack redraws the player skins, your NPC picks that version up. They also appear instantly and work offline. 

## Respawn where they were created

The new default respawn place is **where the NPC was placed**, not where it died. The spot is remembered per character, survives moves and deaths, and never ends up in an export file.

> **About existing worlds:** NPCs whose respawn place was never set by hand will switch to their creation point - for ones already placed, that's wherever they stand now. If you want the old behaviour for someone, pick "Where it died" in their respawn settings.

## Animation and resource packs

- **Bends in emotes.** With bendy-lib installed, NPCs bend their knees, elbows and torso in Emotecraft animations, exactly like the player next to them. Limbs used to stay straight no matter how expressive the gesture was.

releases.notes: # Without Honor: NPCs, Update 0.9.7 Companions got their own animals - mounts and a guardian wolf - weapons in an NPC's hands finally behave honestly, and a heap of bugs got fixed, plus a few fresh ones (that part's a joke... probably). > **Important:** the network protocol version was bumped. Client and server must run the same mod version, otherwise the connection is refused - but nothing breaks silently anymore. ## 🐺 Pets An NPC can summon an animal of its own and ride it while escorting you. - **A mount** - horse, mule, donkey, camel or strider. It shows up when you get in the saddle yourself and leaves a couple of seconds after you dismount. - **Its own horse, not a clone** - every summoned animal has its own coat and its own stats. You can take a snapshot of a real horse with the Memorion Feather and hand it over, or reroll the coat right in the editor. - **Mounted combat** - archers and throwers work straight from the saddle. Everyone else dismounts, fights, and climbs back up. - **A guardian wolf** - comes for the fight, fights beside its owner, and leaves when it's over. Toggled separately from the mount; pick its collar colour with the swatch in the editor. - **Second seat on a camel** - the companion rides along with you if the seat is free. It won't elbow out a real player: it waits a second and a half in case someone wants to sit. **🐣 More settings for pets are coming down the line.** ## Weapons now carry weight - **Attack speed comes from the weapon.** Sword, axe, bare hands - each has its own rhythm, just like a player. An axe hits hard and slow, bare hands fast and weak. - **Manual override** - set a number instead of the automatic value if you want a specific rhythm. - **"From weapon" toggle** - turn it off and damage and speed come strictly from the profile, as before. > **On balance:** this noticeably changes the combat rhythm of NPCs you have ALREADY placed. Unarmed ones will hit more often, axe fighters less often, swordsmen stay as they were. If that breaks the intent for a particular character, untick "from weapon" in its combat settings. ## Dialogues - **"Go to dialogue"** - an action that moves the conversation into another dialogue. - **"Break the button"** - a reply can be locked behind a lock that's knocked off by hitting it. The player holds LMB, cracks spread across the button, and the sound and debris depend on the material. Durability is configurable and the result can be remembered for good. ## Traits and looks - **Fear auras** - the cat one scares creepers, the wolf one drives off skeletons, rabbits and foxes. They combine with any creature type. - **"Doesn't burn"** - fire and lava neither ignite nor hurt. - **"Uses portals"** - it will step into a portal on its own and travel with you to another world while escorting you. Companions used to be left behind at the portal - now they arrive next to you with a teleport effect. - **The Combat tab was rebuilt** - everything fits without scrolling, buttons align to the grid, and "Creature type" moved in with the other submenus. - **The clone book** shows presets under their own names (Cyrillic and CJK are finally visible) with the character's head in the row. - **The damage cap** is raised to 2048. ## Fixed - **The clone book and import "just stopped working".** A single preset with a URL skin was enough to silently kill the whole list - along with import and the second-character picker. Traced to the root and closed, and no network failure disappears without a trace anymore. - **Equipment and accessories went missing.** Export to PC didn't put items in the file, import from PC didn't apply them, the export command overwrote them, and importing a preset without accessories wiped them off a live NPC. Every path now goes through one proven route. ...
